newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cattle farmers demonstrate for EU aid.
newsitem.headline: French cattle farmers demonstrate for EU aid.

text.p: More than 10,000 cattle breeders demonstrated in this central French town on Friday, demanding state and European Union aid to overcome falling sales following the mad cow crisis.

Coming from across central France, they drove tractors through the town to draw attention to their plight and put pressure on EU farm ministers due to discuss compensation for cattle farmers at a meeting in Brussels on Monday and Tuesday.
Christiane Lambert, head of the Young Farmers Union (CNJA), said they chose Clermont-Ferrand, in mountainous Auvergne, to highlight the problems of poor regions whose only resource is pasture.
"These men have grass, and grass is all they have," she said.
There was another demonstration in the southwest city of Toulouse where protesters walled up the local state tax office.
Farmers say calves sell for 3,000 francs ($600), down from 5,000 francs before the mad cow scare, and want the loss to be compensated. They also demand a halt to meat imports from outside the Union.
They say demand for beef has slid by 15 to 20 percent since reports that the mad cow disease, known as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could spread to humans.
"We are demonstrating so that France and Europe come to the rescue," said Luc Guyau, head of the Federation of Farmers Unions (FNSEA).
He called for EU action to revive the meat market and avoid a wave of bankruptcy among farmers.
He said a ban on imports of animal feed from Britain should have reassured consumers, and FNSEA was opening 30,000 breeding farms to the public to show how animals were being fed and bred.
"Consumers have the right to know," Guyau told RTL radio.
Cattle farmers met President Jacques Chirac earlier this week for the second time in less than two weeks to secure sympathy for their plight.
